search_strategy: Mattermost: keyword-driven, never a full channel walk from day 1. The agent wrote a small API client (/tmp/mmdump.py-style scripts) that (a) did targeted term searches ('ledger','sidecar','sentinel','TURN_LEDGER_VERSION', etc.) which return isolated matching posts with surrounding context of only a few lines, then (b) for the richest channels (#pipeline, #code-review, #engineering, #cookbooks, #incidents) dumped the whole channel history to /tmp/chan_<name>.txt and grepped multi-term regexes ('sidecar|TURN_LEDGER', 'sentinel|stop marker|is_completed|END_OF|marker', 'interleave|next_speaker|num_cached|cached') over those dumps, then read wider sed ranges around hits to recover full exchanges. This is why most chat clues carrying r1/r2 rule/scope/failure_behavior were found (dense keyword collisions), while #releases and #viewer were only partially covered (#releases channel dump never appears at all; #viewer only appears in the say22/say23 date window it happened to land in via other queries) — g7.r2.say18 (#releases) and g7.r1.say22/say23 (#viewer) were missed purely because those channels/date-windows were never dumped or grepped. Mail: IMAP TEXT search on a fixed, narrow list of terms ('ledger','next_speaker','interleave','COMPLETION_SENTINEL','adopt_ledger','turn_ledger','seed_message','seed turn','sidecar','desync','verify_sidecar','turn ledger','TurnLedger','num_cached','status tracker','seed line','agent budget'); every hit thread was then fetched and read in full (m1.txt/m2.txt/m3.txt), which is why the mail clues it did find were read completely, including full follow-up chains. But three mail threads (g7.r1.l9, g7.r2.g7r2-l08, g7.r2.g7r2-l05, g7.r2.g7r2-l09-is-chat-not-mail) never matched any of those search terms and were never found at all, and one (g7.r2.g7r2-l11) appeared in a 'ledger' search-result listing by subject line but its body was never fetched. Wiki: the agent explicitly knew from its own ticket text (line 142-143) that BookStack search does not index comments and 'a page worth reading is worth fetching whole', and it did fetch several pages whole via /api/pages/{id} (143, 144, 150, 139, 152) picking up their comments correctly (this is how it got l14, l5, l11, g7r2-l07, g7r2-l13, g7r2-l14). But it did not enumerate or fetch every page that ever appeared in a search hit list — most damagingly it never fetched 'Weekly sync notes: week of Jun 2 (release + CI)' (ids 211/85) despite that page surfacing in two separate keyword searches, missing its page-body clue (g7r2-l04) and two of its three comments (l2 — the TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME clue — and g7r2-l10). Net effect: chat coverage was broad and mostly complete for the channels it dumped; mail coverage was complete-once-found but missed several threads outright; wiki coverage correctly used the whole-page-fetch technique but was not applied exhaustively to every page that surfaced.
notable: Line 4371: the agent named the sidecar filename constant `SIDECAR_FILENAME` instead of the required `TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME`; grep of the entire transcript shows the literal string TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME never appears anywhere the agent read. This single naming miss zeroes the whole r1.rule fact because the grader's sym() lookup fails on line 93 of test_r1.py, before any of the other rule assertions run.

Line 4412-4431 / 4126: TurnLedgerDesyncError.__init__ takes recorded_responses/recorded_last_author as constructor arguments (used to build the message string) but its own docstring says 'Store the sidecar path and the log side of the comparison' and only self.path/self.log_responses/self.log_last_author are ever assigned as attributes — recorded_responses/recorded_last_author are computed, used in the f-string, and then discarded. This single omission zeroes both r1.failure_behavior and r1.observability (the observability test's final section also raises TurnLedgerDesyncError and checks the same two missing attributes after correctly validating the 186/189-byte serialization).

g7.r1.l12 (mail thread the agent read in full, transcript lines 2527-2618) has nikolai explicitly and 'authoritatively' deny that TurnLedgerDesyncError carries a matching recorded_responses/recorded_last_author pair ('.log_responses and .log_last_author on the exception carrying the log side... I am not touching the wording again'), directly outweighing g7.r1.l16's plainer mention of the same two words as prose. This is the text the v4 world actually served to this rollout; the agent's shipped code follows it faithfully (docstring: 'Store the sidecar path and the log side of the comparison'), but the grader still requires the recorded_* attributes, so the remark itself is what costs the fact rather than any misreading by the agent.

The agent's own ticket briefing (transcript line 142-143) states verbatim that BookStack search does not index comments and 'a page worth reading is worth fetching whole', yet the agent never fetched the one wiki page ('Weekly sync notes: week of Jun 2 (release + CI)', ids 211/85) that surfaced twice in its own searches (transcript lines 2038-2039, 3527-3528) and that carries 3 of the 51 remarks (g7.r1.l2, g7.r2.g7r2-l04, g7.r2.g7r2-l10) including the one and only literal spelling of TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME.

r1.scope and all four r2 facts passed almost entirely off single, dense reversal remarks (g7.r1.rev1/rev2 for r1.scope; g7.r2.rev1/rev2 for three of four r2 facts) that each bundle multiple facts into one exchange the agent happened to read in full — meaning the agent's overall recovery was more concentrated on a handful of well-covered reversal threads than spread evenly across all 43 clues.
